title: Quench: single-VM correctness, then V8-v7 performance
constraints: Quench is interpreter-only: one VM core with specializer tiers and exact generic fallbacks; no JIT of any kind (including for comparison runs), executable-memory backend, copy-and-patch stencil, second execution core, or permanent legacy backend.
OXC owns JavaScript syntax; the specializer compiles OXC AST directly to residual bytecode. The JavaScript conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Test262 inventory.

JavaScript and Wasm run on one VM: one heap, one Value representation, one root set, one opcodes! vocabulary, one dispatch loop, one activation stack, and one Engine entry. quench-wasm owns only binary/text decoding, validation and wast scripting; no other crate executes Wasm. The Wasm conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Wasm suite through that shared VM.

Runtime boundary: quench-runtime owns the sole JavaScript/Wasm VM and OXC JavaScript syntax. quench-node is the Node compatibility and host/API layer on top of the runtime public embedding API; Node policy stays out of the runtime. quench-wasm owns Wasm format decoding/validation and wast scripting, and uses the shared runtime for execution. Keep necessary pure algorithms in their single surviving authority. Production hosts and all suite runners use the same core. CLI/runner crate extraction, a new decoded-operator vocabulary, and unrelated package reshuffling are not completion gates. At cutover remove the executable legacy runtime and transitional second-VM names; derive dependency and vendor deletion from actual surviving consumers.

The Node host/API layer remains separate from JavaScript semantics and the Node compatibility gate is 100% of the implemented Node compatibility cases, frozen by task 19 according to implemented capabilities, including existing failures; unimplemented upstream cases are outside this gate. Passing on legacy is not a membership criterion.
Preserve Quench CLI behavior and observable ECMAScript, Node, and Wasm behavior; internal Rust APIs may change.

Guide Stage B with Ershov binding-time analysis, Futamura specialization, and Self VM research on maps, customization, inline caches and type feedback, using the pinned ../v2 source and measured wins/rejections as the implementation reference. Adapt ideas to the single interpreter VM, proven facts or guards with exact fallback, and paired Score/RSS evidence; no sibling build dependency or extra architecture gate.
Production behavior may not select between old and new engines through a runtime flag; pre-cutover comparison uses separate development binaries.

Efficiency completion (task 61, Apple M4/macOS) requires, on each of the eight V8-v7 fixtures, the highest median Score and the lowest median maximum RSS among Quench, QuickJS, Bun/JSC with its JIT disabled, and Node/V8 --jitless. Consult pinned v2 measurements only when they explain a measured gap; no separate parity campaign is required.
Completed task specifications remain in tasks/ with status done and a short completion record; Git history is the archive for progress logs and deleted legacy implementation material.

Only two stages are active: A_correctness ends at task 86 after integrated correctness (24), production cutover and legacy removal (27), and audited cleanup plus final three-inventory verification (86); B_performance begins only after 86 and ends at 28 with task 61 performance qualification.

Use Lisp mindset throughout both stages: one authority per fact, shared semantics, derived state, explicit effects, and exact generic fallback. There is no separate mandatory restructuring or kernel-watermark stage.

During ordinary changes, run only affected Test262 stages and compare-runs against the matching recorded inventory; full suite runs are reserved for gates 24/27 and stage transitions. Apply equivalent affected-scope checks to Node and Wasm. Never shrink inventories, modify suite expectations, or count empty discoveries as passes.

Stage B candidate tasks are optional mechanisms, selected by measured gaps and retained only with paired Score/RSS evidence and correctness checks. Tasks 61 and 28 do not require completion of every candidate or v2 parity.

Unit tests cover internal invariants or scenarios not covered by the pinned Test262, Wasm or implemented Node suites. Retain complicated regression tests only for their distinct internal or uncovered obligation. Remove duplicate language/API/suite-case unit tests; a regression label or multiple execution modes alone do not justify duplicating conformance coverage. Keep suite inventories and assertions unchanged.

The deferred lane is outside the current two-stage plan, non-blocking, and not a third stage. Retain truthful statuses; no active stage depends on deferred work. The only active framework work is the 25-case framework-core profile selected from the existing Node parallel manifest for Express, Koa and Fastify; tasks 88/89's broad inventory and seven-framework gate are superseded.

Reuse final gate reports when production source, binary, configuration and exact inventories are unchanged; recording completion alone never requires another full run. Changed implementations require affected-scope verification and refreshed final stage qualification.

Stage A work is limited to the three frozen inventories (Test262, Wasm, implemented Node cases), one production OXC/Wasm VM in quench-runtime, and removal of legacy/clutter and duplicate suite unit tests. Prioritize concrete failing cases, missing shared-VM execution paths and cutover blockers; implement no discretionary architecture or new host capability beyond what the frozen inventories require. Tasks 20/22/23 own behavior gaps and affected-scope checks; task 24 alone owns the initial same-build 100% qualification and baseline for all three inventories. A gate failure reopens the responsible owner. Task 27 removes legacy, and task 86 qualifies the cleaned build. After 86 passes, proceed directly through 62 and 61 to per-benchmark Score/maximum-RSS qualification.

Phase task lists identify ownership, not mandatory implementation checklists. Suite closures depend on their inventory and shared-VM integration; support tasks supply required fixes and internal checks without imposing their historical plans. Only the Stage A gate enables Stage B; unused optimization candidates never block final qualification.

A_correctness.goal: One production VM for OXC and Wasm; remove all legacy code and audited clutter; retain unit tests only for internals or scenarios not covered by the conformance suites; pass 100% pinned Test262, 100% pinned Wasm directives, and 100% of the frozen implemented Node compatibility cases on the final cleaned build

B_performance.goal: After Stage A is verified, run every V8-v7 benchmark on Apple M4/macOS and achieve the highest Score and lowest maximum RSS against QuickJS, Bun/JSC with JIT disabled, and Node/V8 --jitless; choose mechanisms only from measured gaps
